title: Execution-Signature Recycling: Deduplicating Unit-Test Failure Feedback for Test-Time Code Scaling

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to reduce redundant execution feedback across candidates in best-of-N code generation. Paper [5] ("ModeX: Evaluator-Free Best-of-N Selection for Open-Ended Generation") shares a substantively equivalent purpose, as it aims to improve best-of-N selection efficiency by reducing reliance on external evaluators and optimizing inference-time selection strategies. While the specific mechanism differs, the overarching goal of optimizing best-of-N generation by reducing redundancy aligns.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Execution-Signature Recycling (ESR), clusters candidate programs by their execution signature (sets of failing tests and error types) and conditions subsequent generations on a deduplicated failure bank in a two-round exploration/exploitation procedure. Paper [6] ("Software Behavior and Failure Clustering: An Empirical Study of Fault Causality") describes clustering executions based on internal execution events (e.g., statement profiles) to categorize faulty behaviors, which is substantively equivalent to clustering based on execution signatures. Additionally, Paper [28] ("Igor: Crash Deduplication Through Root-Cause Clustering") employs clustering techniques to deduplicate crash reports based on root causes, which aligns with the deduplication aspect of ESR. Both papers share the underlying primitive of clustering execution data to reduce redundancy.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses HumanEval+ with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct under a 16-generation budget, measuring Pass@1. Paper [17] ("HumanEval-XL: A Multilingual Code Generation Benchmark for Cross-lingual Natural Language Generalization") uses the HumanEval benchmark family, which matches the evaluation design. While HumanEval+ is a specific instance, the benchmark family and metric semantics (Pass@1) are shared, making the evaluation covered.

### Domain
The domain is test-time scaling/inference-time compute for code generation. Paper [7] ("Natural Language to Code Translation with Execution") operates in the same general application area of code generation, as does Paper [10] ("PerfCodeGen: Improving Performance of LLM Generated Code with Execution Feedback"). Both papers address inference-time strategies for code generation, making the domain covered.

## Purpose: Reduce redundant execution feedback across candidates in best-of-N code generation

Looking for papers that aim to reduce redundancy in execution feedback when generating multiple code candidates. Paper [16] (Majority Voting for Code Generation) uses runtime execution signatures across multiple generations to identify representative solutions — this is about aggregating/deduplicating execution results across candidates. Paper [20] (Fast Best-of-N Decoding via Speculative Rejection) aims to reduce wasted computation in best-of-N generation. Paper [7] (Natural Language to Code Translation with Execution) selects among multiple generated programs using execution results. None of these specifically target *reducing redundant execution feedback* across candidates — [16] uses signatures for voting/selection, not to reduce redundancy in feedback. Paper [20] reduces compute waste but not execution feedback redundancy. The purpose of deduplicating failure signals to avoid redundant conditioning is not directly covered.

However, [16] does cluster by execution signatures to avoid redundant evaluation — this is close but the purpose is selection, not reducing redundant feedback for subsequent generation. ## Mechanism: Execution-Signature Recycling — clusters candidates by (failing tests + error types), deduplicates into a failure bank, conditions subsequent generation in two-round explore/exploit

Paper [16] uses "runtime execution signatures on test inputs" to cluster/group programs for majority voting. This is the same primitive of grouping by execution signature. However, [16] uses it for selection, not for conditioning subsequent generation with a deduplicated failure bank. Paper [7] uses execution results to filter/select programs. Paper [30] (Self-Debugging) uses execution feedback to condition subsequent generation. Paper [19] uses self-generated tests with execution feedback for iterative debugging. Paper [24] uses execution semantics for RL-based code generation. The specific combination of: (1) clustering by execution signature, (2) building a deduplicated failure bank, (3) two-round explore/exploit conditioning — this combination is not present. [16] covers the clustering-by-execution-signature primitive. The "deduplicated failure bank conditioning subsequent generation" aspect is not covered. The mechanism is partially covered by [16] for the clustering primitive, but the overall ESR mechanism (deduplication + failure bank + two-round conditioning) is not substantively equivalent to any single prior paper.

## Evaluation: HumanEval+ with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, 16-generation budget, Pass@1

HumanEval is a well-established benchmark family used in many prior papers. Papers [21], [17], [26] use HumanEval variants. Pass@1 is used in [7], [16], [21], and others. The evaluation design (HumanEval benchmark family + Pass@k metric) is covered by multiple prior papers. [16] specifically evaluates code generation with execution signatures using Pass@1 on coding benchmarks.

## Domain: Test-time scaling / inference-time compute for code generation

Paper [16] explicitly works on test-time inference strategy for code generation. Paper [20] works on inference-time alignment (best-of-N). Paper [7] works on code generation with execution at inference time. This domain is clearly covered.
